name: flowly
description: Read the current Paseo Kanban card and its external inputs (Jira, Confluence, GitHub, GitLab), report progress and blockers, propose follow-up ideas, record its input and output artifacts, tag it by module and direction, set its type when missing, keep its workpad of acceptance criteria and checks current, suggest the user's next message, and update its business status through scoped MCP tools or the supplied CLI.
---

# Flowly

Use this skill when working in the workspace of an attached Flowly card.

- Read flowly_get_task before starting a work phase and before reporting after long work. The connection identifies your card/session. Do not choose another card or infer the task from cwd, title, or labels.
- Follow scope.repoPaths and scope.directories. New cards work at the native Paseo project root, which may contain child repositories managed by the user. Older cards can retain a read-only legacy scope; follow the listed directories. A worktree isolates the Git project root only. Provider permissions still apply. Report denied access.
- When work actually starts, set the work stage that matches it: design (plans, specs, research), development (implementation) or test (verification). You decide from the instructions whether to start with design or go straight to development. Keep the stage current as the work changes: switch to development as soon as you start changing code, to test when you verify, and back when needed; never deliver implementation work from design. Report checkpoints and individual contributions with flowly_report_progress. A single session finishing its part does not prove the whole card is finished.
- When you need the user to decide or answer something, ask through your own question tool when you have one (Claude AskUserQuestion, Codex or Pi ask-user): give each question its options, put independent decisions in one call, wait for the answer and continue in the same turn. Flowly shows the card as "Needs you" and the user answers right on the card or in the session. Otherwise (no such tool, an open-ended question that needs a written reply, or a decision the user may take long over) report kind=question with one clear question (offer options when you can), then end your turn; the card shows "Needs you" and the user's reply starts your next turn. Ask each question one way only: never also report a question you asked through your tool, because an answer in the tool starts no new turn and the report would stay open as a second "Needs you". Starting a turn after a user message also moves the card automatically: from in_review to development (review feedback is usually rework), from blocked back to its previous work stage. That stage is only a guess: at the start of every turn, compare it with the work you are about to do (for example, rework of the implementation is development) and set the right stage first if it differs.
- At each delivery (in_review), review what you noticed that the user did not ask for (bugs, refactors, follow-ups) and propose up to 3 with flowly_propose_idea; zero is fine when nothing is worth it, but decide on purpose: the in_review result reminds you when this session has proposed none on the card. Set scope=here for an extension of this card's goal that this card's session can continue with its current context (the user may send it back to this session as an instruction), and scope=new for divergent work that deserves its own card (a bug found on the way, a refactor, a separate feature). Work this card already requires is not an idea; do it. Check ideas in get_task first to avoid duplicates. Put the files, branches and findings a new card would need in context: its agent cannot see this conversation. Ideas are suggestions only; never start one or create cards yourself. If it returns IDEAS_DISABLED, the user turned Ideas off: mention those next steps in your reply instead and do not retry.
- Every turn that delivers (in_review), asks (kind=question) or reports a result (kind=result) ends with next moves (verify the change, commit and push, continue with the next stage, fix what you just found, answer your question); skip them only when nothing needs the user. Put them in the call that ends the turn: pass nextMoves to flowly_update_status when you deliver (in_review), and to flowly_report_progress when you ask (kind=question), report a blocker or give a result. nextMoves holds the 1-3 messages the user is most likely to send you next, recommended first: each a short label in the user's language and the full prompt written as the user's instruction to you. Pass nextMoves: [] (CLI: --no-moves) when nothing needs the user, so that choice is on record; leaving it out records nothing, and the result of that call then carries a reminder. Flowly shows them above the message box; picking one only fills it in and the user sends it. They expire when the user's next message starts a turn; a later nextMoves or flowly_suggest_next_moves call in the same turn replaces them. Use flowly_suggest_next_moves for an update in the middle of a turn or when your delivery call had none. A call that returns an error records nothing, so resend it with the same nextMoves. Still mention the options in your reply. When the whole card is delivered to In review, its changes are committed and pushed (or nothing needed committing) and no issue or user decision remains, you may add one move with moveTo="done" (no prompt, label in the user's language, such as "Move to Done"; it is only accepted together with in_review): picking it moves the card to Done, a decision only the user makes; never add it while changes are uncommitted or unpushed, checks are unrun or something is open. The question itself goes through your question tool or kind=question (with kind=question its nextMoves are the likely answers; a question asked through your tool needs none), and divergent work through flowly_propose_idea, not next moves.
- The result of flowly_update_status (in_review or blocked) and flowly_report_progress (kind=question or result) may carry a reminders array: text naming a call you left out this turn (next moves, or ideas on a delivery). It is never an error and the write already succeeded; make the call before you end the turn, or decide on purpose not to. A result without reminders needs nothing.
- links in flowly_get_task lists cards linked to yours (follow_up_of, follow_up, blocks, blocked_by, related) with their lane; you only see their title and status. If a blocked_by card is not resolved, say so before starting and follow the user's direction; it is a hint, not a reason to set blocked by itself. You cannot create or remove links.
- artifacts in flowly_get_task lists the card's inputs (material it works from) and outputs (deliverables so far), each marked createdBy user or agent. Inputs the user added are part of the task: read every one before you start (files through absolutePath, links with your web tool when you have one), and treat its note as an instruction about how to use it. unread=true marks artifacts added or edited since this session last read the card; at the start of every turn read flowly_get_task and handle unread inputs first. If an input cannot be read (missing, link unreachable or behind a login, no web access), say so in your reply instead of guessing its content. When you deliver, name the inputs you used. When you produce a deliverable (a spec, report, exported file, PR link, verification evidence), register it with flowly_add_artifact role=output; register an outside document or link you relied on as role=input. Do not register every source file you changed; the workspace diff shows them. You may remove only artifacts an agent added (flowly_remove_artifact). If it returns ARTIFACTS_DISABLED, list the deliverables in your reply instead and do not retry.
- An artifact with an external field is an item the user or an agent attached from a connected service: a Jira ticket, a Confluence page, or a GitHub/GitLab issue, pull request or merge request. It is part of the task's requirements. Its link needs a login, so read it with flowly_read_external (CLI: external --id <artifact id>) before you start, and again whenever get_task marks it unread (its description, page content, comments or new commits changed). Its status is reference only: never set the card stage from it, and never try to change the item; Flowly does not write to these services. To review or continue a pull or merge request, fetch its branch with git (the read result names the branch and head commit; it lists changed files but not the diff). When the item and the user's instructions disagree, follow the user and ask with kind=question if unsure. To read a linked item, first add its link with flowly_add_artifact role=input. If the item cannot be read (EXTERNAL_AUTH, EXTERNAL_UNAVAILABLE), say so instead of guessing its content. When you deliver, name the items you worked from.
- Once you understand the scope, tag the card with flowly_set_tags: 1-4 short lowercase tags for the functional areas it touches (a module such as "drawer" or "session-composer") and the directions it serves ("performance", "a11y", "mobile"). Not the task type, status or priority. Reuse a tag from projectTags in flowly_get_task when one fits instead of inventing a synonym, and adjust the tags if the scope changes. You may remove only tags an agent added. When proposing an idea you may suggest tags for it.
- If task.type is missing in flowly_get_task, set it with flowly_set_type once you understand the work: feature (new behavior), bugfix (wrong behavior fixed), research (investigation without a shipped change), refactor (restructuring without behavior change), docs (documentation only) or chore (build, tooling, dependencies, maintenance). Never change a type that is already set; TYPE_ALREADY_SET means the user or an agent chose it, so keep it and do not retry.
- When flowly_get_task lists projectScripts (scripts in the project's paseo.json), run the one that fits what you are about to do with `paseo script start <name>` instead of retyping its commands.
- Keep the card's workpad current with flowly_update_workpad: acceptance criteria, validation checks and confusions. Your plan is read from your own todo list, so keep that list current instead of copying it. Before you start implementing, write the acceptance criteria and the checks you will run; when the card description has a Validation, Test plan or acceptance section, copy each item into the workpad word for word and never weaken or drop one. Each check names the exact command. Update the workpad after each milestone: mark a check pass or fail only after you actually ran it, with the commit it ran on (sha, plus dirty=true when it ran on uncommitted changes); leave it unrun otherwise. Add a confusion when something in the card was unclear and you had to guess. A check that turns out to be unnecessary is removed with a reason in your reply, not marked pass. Copy workpad.revision as workpadRevision; on WORKPAD_CONFLICT the user changed it, so re-read and keep their checks. Before delivering to in_review, rerun checks that are out of date (fresh=stale). If items are still open, the status update returns WORKPAD_OPEN: deliver only with acknowledgeOpen=true and a note that explains every open item. When get_task shows workpadEnabled=false (the call returns WORKPAD_DISABLED), the user turned the workpad off for this project: list the acceptance criteria and checks (passed, failed, not run) in your progress and delivery notes instead and do not retry.
- Use blocked only when the overall task cannot proceed; otherwise report kind=blocker with its impact and the required input. Resume with the work stage you continue in. Deliver the overall result to in_review, explaining changes, verification, unrun checks and remaining issues; the workpad shows them on the card, so keep it and your note consistent. Done/Cancelled/Backlog/Todo are human decisions. The project's lanes define its workflow: only use statuses listed in allowedStatuses, and refer to lanes by their names in lanes.
- Copy revision.task/project and the complete request object into each write. Do not edit signed fields. A progress note does not change task revision; status changes and human edits do. Project edits also invalidate an old context.
- For REVISION_CONFLICT or REQUEST_EXPIRED, re-read and decide whether the intended action is still valid. Never just replace revisions and overwrite the human's work.
- For uncertain timeout/disconnection, repeat the same request and parameters to obtain its receipt. A replay acknowledges the original commit, not that its old status is still current. Never blindly generate a new request to repeat an uncertain write.
- Prefer the MCP tools when present. Otherwise use the supplied absolute CLI/context-file command. Run current --save-request <your-private-snapshot-file>, then status <state> or note with --request-file pointing to that snapshot and a nonempty --note (both also take --moves '<JSON array of {label, prompt} or {label, moveTo:"done"}>' or --no-moves, the next steps for the user), or idea with --request-file, --title, --detail, --rationale and optional --context/--type/--priority/--scope, or artifact with --request-file, --role input|output, --target and optional --title/--note, or artifact-remove with --request-file and --id, or tags with --request-file and --add/--remove (comma-separated), or set-type <type> with --request-file, or next-moves with --request-file and --moves '<JSON array of {label, prompt} or {label, moveTo:"done"}>', or workpad with --request-file, --workpad-revision and --workpad '<JSON {acceptance, validation, confusions}>' (or --workpad-file <path>), or status in_review with --acknowledge-open to deliver despite open workpad items, or external --id <artifact id> to read an external input (no request file). After success save a fresh current snapshot before the next write. Do not reuse a snapshot for a different action after it committed.
- If tools are unavailable, explain the limitation in your reply; do not assert that a card transition succeeded. Never edit board.json, tool credentials, global MCP configuration or another session's context file to work around an error.
- Session running/idle/turn completion is independent of card business status. Do not automatically hand off, assign another agent, or complete the project.
